summary.text: Ayanna Pressley is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 7th District and is unopposed in the November 3 general election. A former congressional and Senate aide, she served on the Boston City Council from 2010 to 2019 and won her House seat in 2018 by defeating incumbent Michael Capuano in the Democratic primary. She is the first Black woman elected to the House from Massachusetts.

paragraphs.text: Pressley was born in Cincinnati, Ohio, in 1974 (February 3, according to Wikipedia) and grew up in Chicago, Illinois.
She attended Boston University from 1992 to 1994.

Before entering elected office she worked as a senior aide to Congressman Joseph P. Kennedy II and Senator John Kerry; according to Wikipedia, she was Kennedy's scheduler and constituency director and Kerry's political director.

Pressley served on the Boston City Council from 2010 to 2019 as an at-large member, and was the first Black woman elected to that body; her congressional office describes her as the first woman of color elected to the council in its 100-year history.

In 2018 she was elected to the U.S. House after defeating ten-term incumbent Michael Capuano in the Democratic primary, and she took office January 3, 2019, as the first Black woman elected to Congress from Massachusetts.
In the House, Pressley serves on the Financial Services Committee and the Oversight Committee, according to her official biography.
In 2020 she publicly disclosed that she lives with alopecia, and according to her office she has since worked to raise awareness of the condition.
